items: **Existing thread:** Mazi answered **Tunahan** on LinkedIn (Jun 24, 2026) and gave his email — Tunahan is the warm sender.

**Systems biology:** Mazi is described as a **systems physiologist**; Tunahan's research is computational systems biology and genome-scale metabolic modelling (PhD on yeast metabolism, guest PhD at DTU with Jens Nielsen). Saliha's PhD is also in bioinformatics and systems biology.

**Metabolism:** Mazi built target discovery for **gastrointestinal, metabolic and liver diseases** (Second Genome) and ran research at January AI (metabolic health). Tunahan maps transcriptome and proteome data onto **metabolic networks**.

**Host and microbe biology:** Saliha's PhD produced a **pathogen–host interaction database** (PHISTO) and Tunahan works on pathogen–host interactions and microbial metabolic models; Mazi's Second Genome work was in the gut.
No shared employer, school, co-author or event was found.

lead_with.title: Ask for advice, not a purchase
lead_with.text: He said no immediate needs. Ask for his view as an **SAB chair and former CSO**: where do multi-omics (DNA + RNA) analysis and AI help most in translational and preclinical work today?

lead_with.text: Since buying **TransCure** (Jan 2026), Taconic runs in vivo studies with immune profiling and flow cytometry. Ask whether **RNA-seq interpretation** of those studies is done in-house or outsourced — PhiTech's biopharma offer covers biomarker identification and patient stratification.

lead_with.title: Ask for the right door
lead_with.text: Mazi knows biotech R&D leaders (NGM, Second Genome, Applied Molecular Transport, January AI). Ask who in his network works on **rare disease or hereditary cancer** — PhiTech's core — and whether he would introduce Saliha.

person.name: Mazi Saberi
person.text: Chairman of Taconic Biosciences' Scientific Advisory Board. A systems physiologist with a record in target discovery and product development across therapeutics, nutraceuticals and digital health. Most recently **Chief Scientific Officer at January AI** (research, clinical development, regulatory, product). Before that, VP and Head of Biology at **Applied Molecular Transport** (several candidates to the clinic), Head of Research at **Second Genome** (target discovery for GI, metabolic and liver diseases), and early career at **NGM Biopharmaceuticals** (South San Francisco), supporting programs that led to multiple INDs. His Streak email and LinkedIn search result point to **Thornhill** (Thornhill Therapeutics) as his current company — not confirmed on the public web.

company.text: Taconic Biosciences (founded 1952 as Taconic Farms) supplies genetically engineered and selectively bred mouse and rat models, humanized immune system (HIS) mice, microbiome models, and model design and breeding services, with three service labs and six breeding sites in the US and Europe. CEO **Mike Garrett**. In August 2025 it became exclusive North America/Europe distributor of **Cyagen's 16,000+ mouse model library**. In January 2026 it acquired **TransCure bioServices** (France), adding in vivo pharmacology, immune profiling, flow cytometry and imaging; TransCure's Sebastien Tabruyn is now President of TransCure and Taconic's Head of Innovation.

financials.text: **2023 revenue:** US$259M. **Ownership:** H.I.G. Capital bought Taconic in 2019; **Avista Capital Partners** acquired it in 2022. No newer figures are public. Growth is coming through deals (Cyagen distribution, TransCure acquisition).

industry.title: Humanized models consolidate
industry.text: Taconic says the TransCure deal creates a single global platform for humanized models, cohort generation and in vivo studies — model suppliers are becoming full study partners, which generates more omics data to interpret.

industry.title: Bigger model libraries
industry.text: The Cyagen deal adds 16,000+ engineered lines (incl. 200+ Cre models) to Taconic's own ~4,500 models.

talking_points: As SAB chair, which scientific bets is Taconic making next — humanized immunity, microbiome, or data services?
After TransCure, who interprets the transcriptomic data from Taconic's in vivo studies — in-house teams, the client, or a partner?
From your time at Second Genome and January AI: where did combining DNA and RNA data change a decision?
What are you building now at Thornhill — and does it touch genomics or RNA analysis?
Who in your network leads rare-disease or hereditary-cancer programs and would value faster DNA + RNA diagnosis?
